markets.note: Miners carried a flat market while every big bank closed lower. Brent fell 17% last week, its steepest weekly drop since the start of COVID.

lead.headline: Trump's midterm rout turns into a fight over Hegseth
lead.body: After a crushing defeat in last week's US midterms, Congress has given Donald Trump an ultimatum: fire Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth or face impeachment proceedings. Republicans are now split over whether to stick with Trumpism for his final two years. Analysts credit the Iran war and living costs for the swing.
lead.why: A weakened White House changes the outlook for the Iran war, AUKUS, tariffs, and the AI boom that has carried markets.

lead.headline: Rate pain lands on Chalmers as Labor turns on itself
lead.body: Mortgage holders have absorbed five RBA hikes this year, taking the cash rate to 4.85%. Environment Minister Murray Watt has told colleagues to stop undermining Treasurer Jim Chalmers after a budget savings meeting. The Coalition is weighing Andrew Hastie as leader to take on Labor and a surging One Nation.
lead.why: Mortgage costs, the budget update, and the next federal election all hinge on whether inflation turns before the RBA does more.

lead.headline: Victorian Labor polls 18%, behind One Nation, with three weeks to go
lead.body: A new poll has Labor at an all-time low of 18%, behind One Nation on 21% and the Coalition on 33%, ahead of the 28 November state election. At the same time the Big Build royal commission heard the CFMEU 'enjoyed a significant level of influence' over the government. NSW Premier Chris Minns called a One Nation candidate's 'demographic replacement' claim racist.
lead.why: If those numbers hold it would be a historic collapse, and One Nation's rise is now reshaping both major parties federally.

lead.headline: Ukraine sets Russia's second-biggest refinery ablaze on eve of peace talks
lead.body: A Ukrainian drone strike set the Kirishi refinery near St Petersburg on fire, killing a local woman. It came a day before Russian, Ukrainian, and US negotiators meet for their first talks since February.
lead.why: The talks are the first real diplomatic track in nine months; refinery strikes are Kyiv's main lever on Russia's war economy.

lead.headline: Netanyahu's rival Eisenkot gets first shot at forming Israel's government
lead.body: Israel's president has asked former military chief Gadi Eisenkot to form a government after an election left the Knesset deadlocked and Netanyahu's coalition without a majority. Eisenkot is courting Netanyahu's allies and says the country is near a 'point of no return'.
lead.why: The first realistic chance in years of Israel being led by someone other than Netanyahu, with the Gaza and Iran fronts still open.

items.headline: Victoria Barracks stays public after veterans' backlash
items.body: The PM has scrapped the sale of four heritage defence sites, including the Sydney and Melbourne barracks, after an audit recommended selling them. Richard Marles denies defence loses out.

items.headline: TikTok grilled over self-harm content
items.body: David Pocock pressed TikTok executives at the Senate inquiry into the government's Digital Duty of Care bill.

items.headline: Aged care waits stretch to two years
items.body: South Australia has the longest waits for residential aged care beds in the country; families describe 'inhumane' choices.

items.headline: Another AI data centre scrapped after local revolt
items.body: Community opposition has now killed a run of proposed data centres; the ACT Conservation Council wants a moratorium.

items.headline: Bathla collapse leaves workers unpaid and estates half-built
items.body: Former staff of the failed Sydney developer speak out about unpaid wages; buyers face unfinished 'wastelands'.

items.headline: Poland treats Krakow market-square shooting as terrorism
items.body: Six people were killed in the Old Town's main square; the 24-year-old gunman has died in hospital. Two police officers who confronted him are being called heroes.

items.headline: New Zealand faces weeks without a result
items.body: National will be the largest party but neither bloc has a clear win. The final count takes three weeks and coalition talks longer, costing NZ its voice at APEC and COP31.

items.headline: Houthi strike hits Aramco tower in central Riyadh
items.body: BBC Verify confirmed damage to the building in the Saudi capital's financial district as the Houthis launched fresh strikes.

items.headline: ANC records its worst-ever result in South Africa
items.body: Ramaphosa says the verdict must be respected; the party's secretary-general called it 'catastrophic'.

items.headline: Pope Leo rebukes Milei's austerity in Argentina
items.body: On the second leg of his Latin America tour, the Pope said the economy must benefit everyone, in a pointed message to the libertarian president.

items.headline: Iran executes three men over January protests
items.body: The men were convicted of 'armed unrest' following anti-government protests earlier this year.

items.headline: ANZ profit up 23% to $7.3b, shares still fall 3.2%
items.body: Investors looked past the headline to the detail. Banks dragged the ASX; BHP rose 2.4%.

items.headline: Nvidia investigates its own CEO over a Chinese intelligence report
items.body: Jensen Huang admitted an affair with a woman reported to have passed information to Beijing. Nvidia is the biggest single weight in global growth ETFs, so this matters for index funds like GHHF and VDHG.

items.headline: Markets rethink the AI trade after the midterms
items.body: The election result has hardened a political backlash against AI and data centres that investors were already pricing in.

items.headline: RBA flags AI spending as a new inflation risk
items.body: AI investment could lift demand faster than the economy can supply it, keeping inflation sticky.

items.headline: ASIC targets cold-callers pushing super switches
items.body: Unlicensed telemarketers are moving people into riskier schemes; advice firms using them face licence action.

items.headline: Gold Coast beachfront sells for a Queensland record $43m
items.body: A private businessman bought the mansion, beating the state's previous residential record.

items.headline: Brisbane clearance rates sag as rate hikes bite
items.body: Auction clearances in Queensland are weak, although renovator homes are still drawing bidders.

items.headline: El Niño summer threatens another big insurance bill
items.body: Last summer's weather cost more than $385m in claims; insurers expect a hot, dry season.

items.headline: $120,000 buys a 50-year lease in new co-housing model
items.body: An Australian-first Queensland project gives older women secure long-term housing for a one-off payment, as rents outpace pensions.

items.headline: NEJM: prehospital ECLS for refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest
items.body: A trial of starting extracorporeal life support before hospital, with an accompanying editorial on bringing rapid reperfusion to more arrest patients. Directly relevant to your paramedicine background.

items.headline: NEJM: stopping statins in older adults without CVD
items.body: A deprescribing trial testing whether primary-prevention statins can be safely discontinued in older patients.

items.headline: NEJM: pelacarsen outcomes trial in high Lp(a)
items.body: The long-awaited cardiovascular outcomes result for antisense Lp(a) lowering, alongside ziltivekimab (IL-6 inhibition) in atherosclerosis.

items.headline: Grattan: specialist fees 'out of control and getting worse'
items.body: Psychiatrists and dermatologists have the highest out-of-pocket gaps; Grattan wants governments to intervene. Specialist colleges partly agree.

items.headline: Cochrane: pharma payments linked to worse prescribing
items.body: A systematic review found doctors who receive industry gifts or payments prescribe more and less appropriately.

items.headline: RACGP pitches specialist wait-time fix before NSW election
items.body: Four months out from the March poll, GPs want parties to commit to cutting specialist queues.

items.headline: Hepatologists finally agree on a definition of ACLF
items.body: A consensus definition of acute-on-chronic liver failure, after years of competing criteria.

items.headline: 2026 on track to be the hottest year on record
items.body: Scientists released the projection as COP31 opened; Nature reports the 1.5°C target is close to being overshot.

items.headline: Baxdrostat's effect lasts two years after stopping
items.body: Patients with primary aldosteronism stayed in remission long after the aldosterone synthase inhibitor stopped, raising the prospect of a cure for a common cause of hypertension.

items.headline: NASA opens applications for moon astronauts
items.body: A new generation will live and work on the lunar surface; applications close 3 December.

items.headline: Apprentice jockey Izzy Neale critical in Dubbo Hospital
items.body: The 22-year-old rising star was seriously injured in a race fall in western NSW.

items.headline: Four locally trained doctors join the rescue squad
items.body: Eight new members were inducted, including four doctors who trained in the region.

items.headline: Universal preschool funding squeezes country preschools
items.body: Celebrated in Sydney, the model is leaving regional preschools facing a funding shortfall.

opinion.title: Labor will have to change tactics if Andrew Hastie leads the Liberals
opinion.author: Patricia Karvelas
opinion.gist: Hastie would be built to fight One Nation on its own turf, and Labor's playbook isn't ready for it.

opinion.title: Victorian Labor: a 'credibility-free' zone
opinion.author: Dight Canning
opinion.gist: Why federal Labor MPs are keeping their distance from the Allan government.

opinion.title: Interest rate hikes are a crude tool, until you look at the alternatives
opinion.author: Jessica Irvine
opinion.gist: Every other inflation lever is slower, more political, or both.

opinion.title: Donald Trump defied populism to do what was right
opinion.author: Rowan Dean
opinion.gist: A defence of Trump against his critics after the midterms.

opinion.title: What's more powerful than the politics of division? Listening
opinion.author: Julianne Schultz
opinion.gist: The US result shows populism isn't inevitable; what Australia should take from it.

opinion.title: New Zealand's foreign policy could change, but not for weeks
opinion.author: Anna Fifield
opinion.gist: Election limbo leaves our closest neighbour without a voice at APEC and COP.
